messages:
Kamal Patel: Heads-up — I'm landing a Terraform change that adds a secondary set of private subnets for the new gpu-batch pool. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321. Plan looks ok but I noticed a potential ordering issue: route_table_association resources are being created before the TGW attachment finishes, which could transiently blackhole egress for those subnets. Snippet from the module:
```
resource "aws_route_table_association" "gpu_private_rt_assoc" {
  subnet_id      = aws_subnet.gpu_private[*].id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.private.id
}

resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway_attachment" "tgw_attach" {
  # cross-account attachment config...
}
```
Anyone seen this in practice? Should I add an explicit `depends_on` on the assoc, split the apply, or is there a better pattern? Also, should the new subnets host the PrivateLink interface endpoints (S3) or keep them in shared-services to avoid extra ENIs on GPU machines?

Lin Zhao: @Kamal I'd add an explicit `depends_on` for the assoc pointing at the tgw attachment while we iterate. We hit the same transient blackhole last quarter. Another pattern is to break the change into two applies: 1) create TGW attachment + endpoints, 2) assoc subnets to the route table. Less pretty but safer. For endpoints, keep them in shared-services unless you need the latency/zone locality — ENIs on GPU hosts can be noisy. :+1:

Anya Morales: FWIW the plan showed a `count` change on aws_eip for the NAT GW in my local run. We should check the EIP pool ordering — I could see the NAT GW attempting to attach routes before the EIPs are allocated which also leads to weird plan diffs. If you split, create EIPs then NAT then assocs.

terraform-bot: Plan result for branch gpu-subnet-ordering: 0 errors, 3 warnings — warning: "route_table_association may cause temporary blackhole if transit gateway attachment not ready". Full log: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/terraform/plan/4321

Eli Rivera: Another option is to use a small rollout with canary subnets + traffic weigh down to verify rules before full assoc. Tagging @eng-sre in case we want to schedule a short maintenance window.

Kamal Patel: Thanks — I'll split into two PRs (tgw+endpoints first, then subnet assoc) and add a `depends_on` guard in the short term. I'll also validate EIP allocation ordering in the NAT module and keep endpoints in shared-services. Will update the PR with the change and ping when ready for a canary apply. :eyes:
